news.title: Google launches Gemini Decision 1, a specialized AI model
news.description: Google has launched Gemini Decision 1, a low-cost model designed to answer binary, multiple-choice, or rating questions. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and also provides a confidence score.

news.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights
news.description: United Airlines will block unauthorized third-party AI agents that attempt to book, purchase, or manage trips through its channels. The airline cites privacy, account security, and federal aviation regulations, among other reasons.

news.title: AlphaGenome 2 links genetic mutations to cell types
news.description: Google DeepMind has launched AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts the effect of genetic variants on specific types of human cells. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identified about 30% of causal variants, compared with 16% previously.

news.title: AWS offers a free local equivalent of its cloud
news.description: AWS is offering developers a free local equivalent of its cloud services, built by AI agents.

news.title: Nvidia Reportedly Preparing to Fire Jensen Huang After Another Affair
news.description: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to fire CEO Jensen Huang after the Wall Street Journal reported a second affair, this time with another company executive.

news.title: Experts validate OpenAI’s physical proof of Yang-Mills
news.description: Experts appointed by OpenAI have verified its proof of the existence of Yang-Mills quantum theory. However, they do not yet claim to fully understand the proof, which is considered too long and complex for humans to immediately digest.

news.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO
news.description: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and CEO since 1993, resigned after acknowledging affairs with female executives linked to the company. Colette Kress becomes interim CEO, while Nvidia shares fell as much as 14%.

news.title: Starlink limits the speed of Ukrainian drones
news.description: Starshield, Starlink’s military version, is reportedly cutting the satellite connection to Ukrainian equipment traveling faster than 161 km/h again. This limit prevents interceptor drones from pursuing certain Russian drones flying at up to 400 km/h.

news.title: Companies offer high salaries and luxury travel to attract AI talent
news.description: Companies are offering generous compensation and luxury travel to compete for artificial intelligence talent.

news.title: ChatGPT Lets Businesses Claim Their Profiles for Free
news.description: OpenAI is launching Businesses in ChatGPT, a beta space where eligible businesses can claim a verified profile, track their mentions, and create a conversational agent. Profiles are free, but agents are initially available to online retailers and digital services in the United States.

news.title: Claude Launches Sheets, Whiteboards, and Narrated Data Videos
news.description: Anthropic is launching Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, new workspace tools. Claude Data can connect to Snowflake and Salesforce to create dashboards, visual stories, or short narrated videos, while Sheets lets users build spreadsheets and Whiteboards enables collaboration on a shared board.

news.title: Blue Unveils a Smartphone That Manages Apps for the User
news.description: Blue is developing a phone that acts as a chief of staff for apps, handling repetitive tasks and showing only important information. The Y Combinator-backed startup is testing its beta version with former iPhone users.

news.title: Grok Bot becomes a proactive colleague for teams
news.description: With Grok Bot 1.0, the agent can handle tasks without being prompted, retain a shared memory of the organization, and communicate in Slack or Microsoft Teams. It is available now and learns from teams’ feedback and preferences.

news.title: ChatGPT Launches a Personal Finance Tool in Its Desktop App
news.description: ChatGPT’s personal finance tool is available in the desktop app for all plans. It provides personalized answers about users’ money and spending.

news.title: Adobe will open Photoshop and its other Creative Cloud apps to AI assistants
news.description: Adobe plans to let assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude directly modify content in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects through Model Context Protocol integrations. The feature is expected to enter private beta in early 2027 and aims to automate repetitive tasks while preserving manual control.

news.title: Anthropic Signs Up to $4.3 Billion in Cloud Deals with Microsoft
news.description: Anthropic has expanded its cloud computing agreements with Microsoft for up to $4.3 billion. The company is seeking more infrastructure capacity ahead of its planned IPO.

news.title: Anthropic Reportedly Surpasses OpenAI in Revenue with Far Lower Losses
news.description: Anthropic reportedly generated $17 billion in revenue in the third quarter, compared with $10 billion for OpenAI, while posting far lower operating losses. OpenAI is accelerating its enterprise sales and could cut prices to close the gap.

news.title: Google Labs launches Tabletop, AI-generated mini-tools for groups
news.description: Tabletop lets users turn links, files, and ideas into collaborative tools such as an itinerary, a poll, or a tournament bracket. The service is limited to the United States and available by waitlist.

news.title: Companies Are Banning Artificial Intelligence Agents
news.description: Some companies are banning AI agents. The article lists the companies involved.

news.title: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI Add New Tools to Their AI Products
news.description: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI have each added tools designed to move more tasks into their AI products, including Claude’s shared spreadsheets and ChatGPT’s professional agents.

news.title: Mathematicians Seek to Preserve Their Profession Amid AI Advances
news.description: Artificial intelligence is now advancing into high-level mathematical research, forcing the community...

news.title: Part 5: Automating repetitive tasks with AI
news.description: The final part of the playbook explains how to document your system, connect beehiiv to AI, and automate recurring tasks. It also shows how to turn the most engaged readers into customers and build a prompt library.

news.title: Guide: Creating a B2B newsletter that generates leads
news.description: This guide explains how to write for an ideal customer, use your newsletter as a CRM, and measure leads rather than just opens.

news.title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production through summer 2027
news.description: Tesla will continue producing the Cybertruck through the end of summer 2027 to clear its order backlog, according to Elon Musk. The lineup has been reduced to the Cyberbeast alone, priced at around $110,000.

news.title: Roku abandons its smart home ambitions
news.description: Roku is abandoning its ambitions in the smart home sector.

news.title: IBM aims to link two quantum chips to reach 1,040 qubits
news.description: IBM plans to link two quantum chips to create a 1,040-qubit system in 2027.

news.title: Helsing launches Clarity, a European rival to Palantir’s Maven
news.description: Helsing is launching Clarity, a European solution presented as a rival to Palantir’s Maven.

news.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI exposes Notion conversations
news.description: A cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access transcripts of conversations involving Notion customers.

news.title: Gemini comes to Apple CarPlay
news.description: Gemini is now available on Apple CarPlay.

news.title: Reddit resisted U.S. and German demands to identify users
news.description: Reddit rejected attempts by U.S. and German authorities to unmask certain users.

news.title: Apple HomeView: A limited but promising launch
news.description: An analysis of Apple HomeView describes a limited launch with significant potential.

news.title: Howard Lutnick does not want to halt Nvidia chip exports
news.description: Howard Lutnick reportedly does not want to stop the flow of Nvidia chips overseas.

news.title: Complex AI agent architectures cost up to 4.7 times more
news.description: An analysis of agents designed for professional workflows finds no dominant design. Multi-step architectures cost up to 4.7 times more and introduce up to 5.8 times more latency, with gains that are rarely sufficient.

news.title: Studies on AI medical scribes use 96 different metrics
news.description: AI medical scribes are evaluated using 96 metrics across 54 studies, one-third of which are used by only a single study. The results are therefore difficult to compare and rarely account for safety or patient outcomes.

news.title: Processing underrepresented languages can cost up to ten times more
news.description: Models charge up to ten times more to process underrepresented languages such as Amharic. A Portuguese-designed vocabulary reduces costs for Guarani and Quechua by about 24%.

news.title: One-third of U.S. adults have left an online community
news.description: According to a Pew Research Center survey, about one-third of U.S. adults say they have left an online community. More than eight in ten cite declining interest.

news.title: Adobe Adds Video, Music, and Sound Generation to Premiere
news.description: Adobe is adding tools to Premiere for generating video, sound effects, ambience, and music directly in the timeline. These tools rely on models from Adobe Firefly, Google, Kling, Runway, and Luma.

news.title: Google Makes Gemini 4 Carbon Available After Limited Rollout
news.description: Google has made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available after a two-week limited rollout to cybersecurity advocates. The model is accessible through Gemini, AI Mode in Search, and Antigravity.

news.title: Anthropic Publishes a Guide to Choosing the Right Claude Model
news.description: Anthropic published a guide explaining how to choose the appropriate Claude model for each task. It recommends, among other things, pairing cheaper models with simple tasks and more powerful models with ambitious projects.

news.title: Colette Kress, the CFO Guiding Nvidia Through Its Transition
news.description: The article profiles Colette Kress, the CFO guiding Nvidia through its first leadership transition.

news.title: Who Is Kimberly Powell, the Former Nvidia Executive Linked to Jensen Huang?
news.description: The article profiles Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive accused of having a relationship with CEO Jensen Huang.

news.title: Elon Musk Says He Would Hire Jensen Huang
news.description: Elon Musk said he would hire Jensen Huang.

news.title: China Would Be the Main Beneficiary of Jensen Huang’s Downfall
news.description: The article analyzes why China would be the main beneficiary of Jensen Huang’s downfall.

news.title: Natura Is Preparing a Smart Ring with a Voice Agent
news.description: Natura is developing a steel ring with a button for requesting help, recording ideas, and launching voice agents on nearby devices. It will also track sleep, heart rate, and steps, with a Kickstarter launch and deliveries planned for December or January.

news.title: Three New AI-Powered Scams Exploit Voices, Images, and Personal Data
news.description: Fraudsters are using AI to analyze public posts, clone voices, and create fake images or videos to personalize their attacks. The scams discussed include contextual spear phishing, fake video calls from a CEO, and ransom demands involving supposedly missing pets.

news.title: Yandex Recovers 97% of Data Affected by Drone Attacks
news.description: Russian cloud provider Yandex recovered about 97% of customer data affected by drone strikes on three data centers in October. The remaining 2.84% is permanently lost, and Yandex plans to enable backups by default and strengthen its infrastructure.

news.title: Platform Engineering Must Adapt to AI Agents and Nontechnical Users
news.description: The rise of AI agents and nontechnical creators is pushing platform engineering to manage a mix of human improvisation and precise automation. Platforms must incorporate machine-readable guardrails, limited identities, and Kubernetes-inspired control loops.

news.title: Cisco Will Integrate All Future Products with Its Cloud Control Platform
news.description: Cisco announced that all new products starting in 2027 will integrate with Cloud Control, a unified interface for networking, security, and observability. The service will expand internationally starting in February, while Cisco also plans to simplify ThousandEyes licensing and expand Live Protect.

news.title: IBM and Microsoft Launch Imagine Enterprise to Govern AI Agents
news.description: IBM Consulting and Microsoft launched Imagine Enterprise, an agentic AI platform aimed in part at regulated industries. It combines more than 6,000 preconfigured IBM agents with Microsoft’s Azure, Entra, Purview, Defender, and Sentinel services.

news.title: U.S. Data Center Electricity Demand Is Growing Ten Times Faster Than the Grid
news.description: U.S. data center electricity demand has increased by about 19% annually since 2000, compared with 2% for grid capacity. According to Howden, data centers may need to obtain up to 58% of their electricity off-grid by 2030.

news.title: GraphRAG Improves Knowledge Retrieval for AI Applications
news.description: GraphRAG stores knowledge as interconnected entities and relationships, improving performance over traditional RAG for multistep reasoning and broad summaries. However, this approach incurs significantly higher indexing and processing costs.

news.title: SAP Makes ABAP a Runtime Foundation for Enterprise Agentic AI
news.description: SAP is positioning the ABAP platform as an enterprise runtime foundation for agentic AI as part of its vision for the autonomous enterprise. Upcoming developments include governance, reliability, scaling, and an ABAP Model Context Protocol server.

news.title: Microsoft Reveals a Technique for Hiding a Backdoor in an AI Agent
news.description: Microsoft researchers discovered “Lazarus,” a technique capable of reprogramming dormant neurons in an AI model. An apparently normal agent can then execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

news.title: Thundermail, Thunderbird’s Email Service, Opens Early Access
news.description: Thunderbird has begun offering early access to Thundermail, its paid email-hosting service. It offers custom domains, 30 GB of storage, and integration with Thunderbird’s desktop and mobile apps.

news.title: Ottawa, Kansas, Approves a Ten-Year Moratorium on Data Centers
news.description: Voters in Ottawa approved a ten-year restriction on data centers by nearly 72%.

news.title: ByteDance is preparing a personal AI agent to compete with Meta
news.description: ByteDance is reportedly preparing a personal AI assistant capable of performing tasks such as shopping or managing a schedule. Its name, features, and launch date are not yet known.

news.title: AI Agents Spot a Maya Pyramid in Lidar Images
news.description: Forty-eight AI agents analyzed NASA lidar images covering 1,200 square kilometers of Mexican jungle and identified a site containing a pyramid. However, the site had already been mapped in 2025, contrary to the experiment’s initial claim.

news.title: A Robot Duck Learns to Follow a Cat in a Few Hours
news.description: A Wired journalist used GPT-6 Sol to program and train a virtual version of the Microduck robot to spot and follow their cat. The experiment took a few hours instead of several weeks.

news.title: Adobe Shows Prototypes for 3D Photos and AI Characters
news.description: Adobe presented prototypes that can turn an image into a 3D scene, shape an AI character’s personality through conversation, and simplify photo editing. These tools are not yet commercial products.

news.title: The Authors of “AI 2027” Predict Superhuman AI as Early as 2027
news.description: A METR report estimates that Anthropic is progressing about twice as fast as before, largely thanks to AI. The AI Futures Project now considers it likely that AI surpassing the best human researchers will arrive in 2027.

news.title: TrustedRouter Combines Multiple AI Models, Including a U.S. Version
news.description: TrustedRouter is launching Prometheus 4.0, Liberty 4.0, and Polyphemus 1.0, which combine multiple models or select the best one for each request. Requests can remain encrypted through to the processing server.

news.title: Helsing unveils AI to prepare targets for weapons systems
news.description: Helsing’s Clarity platform turns sensor data into target recommendations. The company says every decision will be attributed to a responsible human and placed under European oversight.

news.title: Researchers warn that AI progress is accelerating
news.description: Two recent reports reportedly indicate that AI is advancing faster than expected, raising concerns especially among Anthropic’s safety researchers. The Information also publishes its annual selection of 50 promising startups.

news.title: 3,500 laser robots eliminate parasites from Norwegian salmon
news.description: In Norwegian fish farms, around 3,500 underwater robots use AI vision to spot sea lice and then eliminate them with lasers. They replace the chemical baths used previously.

news.title: DeepL Voice translates tone, emotion and sarcasm in real time
news.description: DeepL Voice’s Aure model reproduces the speaker’s tone, emotion, emphasis and speaking rate in the target language. It works in eight languages, including French, during meetings, face-to-face conversations and via the API.

news.title: 35,000 applications created with Grok exposed sensitive data
news.description: Claroc discovered more than 35,000 applications generated with Grok that were accessible without logging in. Some contained patient data, plaintext passwords and internal information from SpaceXSI.

news.title: Anthropic ports Claude to AMD chips in three days
news.description: Anthropic says its internal Mythos model enabled it to port Claude to AMD chips in three days, whereas such a migration usually took several months. Claude now runs on four chip families.

news.title: ElevenLabs announces 13 products at once
news.description: According to the AI Secret newsletter, ElevenLabs reportedly presented 13 new products in a single announcement. Details are not yet publicly available.

news.title: Teenager’s parents sue Google after exchanges with Gemini
news.description: According to a lawsuit, a teenager from North Carolina exchanged messages for nearly three months with Google Search’s AI Mode, powered by Gemini, about suicide. Senator Ed Markey is asking Google to allow schools to disable these features.

news.title: DeepSeek’s AI agent reportedly reaches 1.54 million daily users
news.description: This figure comes from the AI Secret newsletter, without an accessible primary source, and has not been confirmed by DeepSeek. If verified, it would show the rapid growth of Chinese AI agents among the general public.

news.title: US brokers reportedly sell training data to China
news.description: A ChinaTalk investigation claims that at least nine US companies sell training data to Chinese laboratories. The data notably includes reinforcement-learning environments, which are largely outside export controls.

news.title: Megaspeed suspected of delivering Nvidia chips to China
news.description: This Singapore-based data-center operator is suspected of moving billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips banned from export into China. Information about $7.5 billion in shipments has not been verified by CNBC.

news.title: Omnii Defense presents offline AI to detect biological weapons
news.description: Startup Radical Numerics presented a tool that runs without internet access on a laptop connected to a USB DNA sequencer. It assigns each sequence a threat score between 0 and 1, but faces criticism related to the departure of its adviser George Church.

news.title: Databricks launches an AI agent that analyzes business problems
news.description: The new version of Genie independently chains together long-running tasks using a company’s internal data. Its CEO uses it in particular to analyze internal surveys, lost sales and prepare for interviews.

news.title: Europe wants to ban dark patterns and loot boxes for minors
news.description: The proposed Digital Fairness Act targets difficult-to-cancel subscriptions, addictive design, ads targeting minors, and personalized pricing, among other practices. Fines could reach 6% of global turnover.

news.title: UK mandates university exams resistant to AI
news.description: The English regulator believes it is nearly impossible to fairly assess work completed at home. Universities will have to return to supervised examinations or face sanctions.

news.title: A $749 kit turns seawater into drinking water
news.description: Vital Lyfe designed a portable desalination unit weighing around 11 kg. It produces 22.7 liters per hour from seawater and can be installed on a boat without drilling through the hull.

news.title: Uber launches a parking-space reservation service
news.description: Uber Parking lets users compare and reserve a space through the SpotHero network, which includes 13,000 parking facilities in 400 cities across the United States and Canada. The service is not yet planned for Europe and currently has no AI component.

news.title: Meta replaces its longtime infrastructure chief
news.description: Santosh Janardhan is stepping down as Meta’s head of infrastructure, where he had worked since 2009, but will remain an adviser during the transition. Dave Brown, formerly Amazon’s head of cloud and AI, will succeed him.

news.title: CoreWeave says demand for AI computing far exceeds supply
news.description: CoreWeave reported better-than-expected results and raised its forecast, sending its stock higher. Its CEO says Nvidia H100 chips bought four years ago are still being re-rented at 20% to 50% above their purchase price.

news.title: Nvidia seeks candidates to replace Jensen Huang
news.description: Nvidia is looking for a potential successor to CEO Jensen Huang following reports of several extramarital affairs. The board is considering appointing an interim executive while searching for a permanent replacement.

news.title: The risk of humanity losing power to superintelligence
news.description: Some AI experts believe that once superintelligence is achieved, humans could permanently lose their power and be governed by an AI. The article argues that it is still possible to steer the technology away from completely replacing human judgment.

news.title: Sub-agents involve different trade-offs depending on their use
news.description: Different methods of delegating to sub-agents fail in different ways, and teaching agents to choose between them is difficult. Forking is often preferable to synthesis, but can become costly as the context grows.

news.title: AI could accelerate both imitation and competitive advantages
news.description: AI can simultaneously accelerate imitation and the accumulation of advantages. The presence of a lasting competitive advantage and the entry price will determine which companies and investors benefit from the technology.

news.title: Social relationships are becoming more valuable in the professional world
news.description: The benefits of being sociable have increased, and many well-connected people blend their professional and personal lives. The article presents authenticity, generosity and curiosity as the best strategy.

news.title: Applications capture the largest share of AI margins
news.description: With an application margin of 40%, applications, neoclouds and inference providers capture 40%, 28% and 24%, respectively, of total gross profit before GPU depreciation. Together, they account for 92% of that profit.

news.title: Agentic engineering levels reveal what is still done manually
news.description: The article proposes looking at the tasks teams still perform manually to identify their level of agentic engineering.

news.title: AI’s current capabilities justify concern
news.description: Current models could already transform science and medicine for decades. Slowing AI research would therefore cost less than one might think.

news.title: Companies treating agents as customers are targeting strong growth
news.description: Companies that regard agents as full-fledged customers could benefit from a new wave of growth.

news.title: Engineering is presented as the answer to AI challenges
news.description: Optimizing incident response times also accelerates development times.

news.title: Startups offer high compensation to recruit AI talent
news.description: AI startup Serval is offering a $30,000 signing bonus and $10,000 in vacation benefits to attract software engineers and deployment specialists.

news.title: U.S. Futures Fall Before the Open
news.description: U.S. stock futures fell on Thursday as turmoil at Nvidia worsened.

news.title: December 23 Could Be the Ideal Day to Buy a Home
news.description: The Christmas period can be particularly favorable for homebuyers. One agent specifically recommends making an offer on December 23.

news.title: Wall Street Fears the Fed Could Go Too Far Against Inflation
news.description: The high October CPI report prompted some Fed officials to adopt a tougher tone. One governor said he favored a 50-basis-point rate hike.

news.title: An Investor Bets on Recycling Data Center Materials
news.description: Tazia Smith, CEO of Closed Loop Capital Management, sees opportunities in companies that help data centers reuse raw materials from their supply chains.

news.title: Standard Bots Wants to Build America’s Robotics Giant
news.description: Standard Bots CEO Evan Beard wants to compete with Chinese robot manufacturers. He is counting in part on vibe coding and support from allies in Washington.

news.title: Google Lets Employees Test Its Gemini Hydrogen Model
news.description: Google is allowing employees to test Hydrogen, a new Gemini model described as faster and more cost-effective. One employee compares it with the company’s previous Flash models.

news.title: Hacker Houses Are Creating Their Own Venture Funds
news.description: Hacker houses want to invest in future unicorns before traditional venture capital funds do. Two former Mission Control roommates have launched Mission Street Capital.

news.title: Deloitte Cuts GLP-1 Drug Coverage for Employees
news.description: Deloitte is reducing coverage of GLP-1 drugs for weight loss for its U.S. employees. The company is also raising the cost of their health insurance.

news.title: Video Game Publishers Benefit from the Return of Classic Franchises
news.description: New Legend of Zelda and World of Warcraft games generated record results for Nintendo and Blizzard. Preorders for Grand Theft Auto 6 also exceeded expectations.

news.title: Rent Exceeds 30% of Income in 31 U.S. States
news.description: In Hawaii and New York, rent accounts for about half of income, compared with roughly 21% in North Dakota. Affordability pressures are spreading beyond traditionally expensive regions.

news.title: Miss Universe Controversies Ahead of TLC Documentary
news.description: The report recaps the controversies surrounding Miss Universe ahead of the release of TLC’s new documentary series, Crown of Deceit.

news.title: Alex Karp Says Palantir Is a Progressive Company
news.description: Alex Karp describes himself as a lifelong Democrat and says Palantir’s products are “essentially progressive.”

news.title: Elon Musk’s Exercise for Identifying Talent
news.description: The article presents the exercise Elon Musk uses to identify talent and explains how to apply it to demonstrate one’s impact at work.

news.title: The Ten U.S. States That Will Build the Most Homes
news.description: The article presents the ten U.S. states expected to build the most homes in the coming years.

news.title: Tesla Will Extend Cybertruck Production Through the End of Summer
news.description: Elon Musk said Tesla would extend Cybertruck production through the end of summer.

news.title: Amanda Seyfried Has No Regrets About Her Scene with Billy Evans
news.description: Amanda Seyfried said she has no regrets about her confrontation with Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’s partner, in a memorable scene.

news.title: Meghan Markle’s Relationship with Her Father Detailed
news.description: The article traces the relationship between Meghan Markle and her father, Thomas Markle.

news.title: xAI Abandons JAX for a C/C++ Stack Ahead of Grok 4.8 Deployment
news.description: Elon Musk says xAI has replaced JAX with an internally developed C and C++ stack. Grok 4.8 is undergoing reinforcement learning ahead of a phased rollout announced for the week.

news.title: IBM Reaches New Milestones Toward Its Starling Quantum Computer
news.description: IBM says it has reached significant milestones toward Starling, its fault-tolerant quantum computer planned for 2029. The company has notably linked two chips with a 1% error rate.

news.title: Meta Dramatically Speeds Up the k-means Clustering Algorithm
news.description: Meta researchers updated k-means to achieve lower error in 1.4 to 2.6 passes instead of 25. They report GPU speedups of 10 to 45 times.

news.title: Microsoft Announces Classroom, Its Autonomous Education Portal
news.description: Microsoft announced Classroom, an autonomous education hub bringing together assignments, grades and Copilot Teach. The service will arrive in 2027 at no additional cost for certain Microsoft 365 A2, A3, A5 and A7 customers.

news.title: ElevenLabs Launches Scribe v3 with Multilingual Live Transcription
news.description: Scribe v3 transcribes audio in 102 languages with 27% fewer word errors than version 2, according to ElevenLabs’ benchmark. Its Live version can now identify speakers in real time.

news.title: Nod, n8n’s Open-Source Personal Agent, Automates Tasks on Computers
news.description: Nod is a personal agent from n8n that runs on a Mac, Windows PC or server. It can follow up on unpaid invoices, cancel trials and prepare a briefing before a call; it is available as a free, open-source research preview.

news.title: Facade Code Lets Multiple Coding Agents Collaborate in VS Code
news.description: Facade Code is a VS Code extension that runs Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents side by side in tabs. It also lets them communicate with one another and is released under the MIT license.

news.title: Switzerland Must Learn to Worry Despite Its Good Health
news.description: Switzerland is doing well, but that may be precisely why it needs to learn to worry.

news.title: Trust and Investment Are Essential to Industrial Survival
news.description: An industry does not disappear overnight: it first stops believing in itself and investing. By the time we realize it, it is often too late, in a world that is fragmenting.

news.title: Magnetic Microrobots Could Speed Up the Dissolution of Blood Clots
news.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich have developed microrobots capable of improving the delivery of drugs to...

news.title: A meeting on the energy technologies of tomorrow has been announced
news.description: On December 8, 2026, from 1:30 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. at Station R in Renens, a meeting...

news.title: ETH Zurich transforms plastic waste into high-performance adhesives
news.description: Researchers at ETH Zurich have developed a method for transforming waste plastic into...

news.title: Empa develops a new generation of antimalarial mosquito nets
news.description: Researchers at Empa have developed a new fiber for making impregnated mosquito nets...

news.title: Quantum vibrations pave the way for future molecular clocks
news.description: Researchers at the University of Basel have succeeded in observing and controlling quantum vibrations...

news.title: Basophils could slow down the first lung metastases
news.description: Immune cells mainly known for their role in allergies may also help to...

news.title: A hot-spring amoeba pushes back the thermal limit of complex life
news.description: An amoeba discovered in a California hot spring has just broken a biological record...
